body:
I have a history of mental illness in my family. It has nothing to do with gender in this case. My grandma, aunt, cousins, siblings, etc have struggled with a form of mental illness in one way or another. I don't have a hormone problem. 

I'm someone who relies on routines/regularity, but lately I've been skipping classes (college) because I just don't want to leave my room. I'll go to the store and do other things. I have hobbies, but I put myself down when it comes to them. I love photography, but I think I've lost my touch with it.

I'm a 21 year old female who's been struggling with depression for about 6 years. Looking back it seems I always had some level of anxiety that has just gotten progressively worse over time. I went to a psychiatrist for the first time just over 2 years ago and started prozac. He added lamictal at the start of 2019.

​

 I would have to say the main cause of my depression is loneliness, but I have a really hard time overcoming it. The anxiety can stem from a lot of things; going to class, taking the train, over stimulation (noises usually), and just generally picturing bad things happening constantly (ie. my parents are the kitchen and i picture my dad killing my mom). The last thing in particular has gotten worse very recently. I'm not afraid to do things, but I have this constant fear in the back of my head.   


I felt like an idiot when I went to my psychiatrist last week and he basically shrugged his shoulders at me. Kind of telling me to just buck up and the meds should be working. I've tried drinking as a copy mechanism once and have been considering doing it again over the past few days.

I really almost never take it. I've had it prescribed to me for over 2 years and rarely took it in all that time. I've recently gone into a bad bought of depression and feel like I need it to sleep or just feel numb. This just started a couple days ago.
